silabus_tekst: RNU study course “Environment, Labour and Civil Protection” description Study program Information Systems Amount 3 CP = 75 ac.h. Author (s) Valentīna Djakona Preliminary knowledge, Related study courses No preliminary knowledge required Aim To acquaint students with basic principles of civil protection, to explain its tasks and an order of legal regulation; to acquaint students with the relevant regulations of the Republic of Latvia; to train the main methods of first-aid treatment; to identify the problems connected with pollution of the environment and use of natural resources, to reveal philosophy and instruments of the modern environmental policy; to acquaint students with the normative legal acts regulating issues of labour protection. Planned Learning Outcomes (PLO) 1. Able to apply the requirements of the regulatory enactments regulating the professional activities of the sector and monitor their implementation. 2. Act in accordance with fire safety, electrical safety, labor protection and environmental protection requirements. 3. Able to comply with civil protection requirements in accordance with civil protection plans and regulatory enactments. 4. Able to act responsibly in an emergency situation and during a state of emergency, observing the regulations set by the state and being aware of their responsibility for maintaining national security, and to provide the necessary first aid. 5. Able to understand the basic labor protection requirements for office employees and organize the work environment in accordance with labor protection and environmental protection requirements. 6. Able to understand the most typical work environment risk factors when working with a computer. Literature and other sources of information: Compulsory reading - Civilās aizsardzības un katastrofas pārvaldīšanas likums (Civil Protection and Disaster Management Law). Publicēts: Latvijas Vēstnesis, 100, 25.05.2016. (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/282333-civilas-aizsardzibas-un- katastrofas-parvaldisanas-likums) - Darba aizsardzības likums (Labour Protection Law). Stājas spēkā: 01.01.2002. Publicēts: Latvijas Vēstnesis, 105, 06.07.2001. (https:// likumi.lv/ta/id/26020-darba-aizsardzibas-likums) - Ministru kabineta noteikumi Nr. 238, Ugunsdrošības noteikumi (Republic of Latvia Cabinet Regulation No. 238 Fire Safety Regulations). Publicēts: Latvijas Vēstnesis, 78, 22.04.2016. (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/281646- ugunsdrosibas-noteikumi) - Ugunsdrošības un ugunsdzēsības likums (Fire Safety and Fire-fighting Law). Publicēts: Latvijas Vēstnesis, 165, 13.11.2002. (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/ 68293-ugunsdrosibas-un-ugunsdzesibas-likums) - Vides aizsardzības likums (Environmental Protection Law). Publicēts: Latvijas Vēstnesis, 183, 15.11.2006. (https://likumi.lv/doc.php?id=147917) Recommended - Verdenhofa, O., Dzenis, O., Dehtjare, J., Djakona, V., Gavkalova, N. "Strategic Management as a Tool for the Development of Public Sphere Entities". Public Policy and Administration, 2024, 23(2), pp. 175-196 - Hunt, G. "Health and Safety Pocket Book" (2nd ed.). Routledge, 2018 - Fury, S. "The Disaster Survival Handbook: A Disaster Survival Guide for Man-Made and Natural Disasters" (Escape, Evasion, and Survival Book 7). Kindle Edition - Eves, D. "Disasters: Learning the Lessons for a Safer World". Routledge, 2018 - Krishna, M., Manickam, V., Shah, A., Davergave, N. "Environmental Management: Science and Engineering for Industry". Butterworth- Heinemann, 2017 - Labklājības ministrijas materiāli (www.lm.gov.lv) - Valsts darba inspekcijas materiāli (www.vdi.gov.lv) - Latvijas Brīvo arodbiedrību savienības materiāli (www.lbas.lv) - Valsts sociālās apdrošināšanas aģentūras materiāli (www.vsaa.lv) - Materiāli (www.osha.lv) - Materiāli (www.likumi.lv) - Nacionālais ugunsdzēsības un glābšanas dienests (http://vugd.gov.lv) Study course content and schedule of contact hours Week Topic Academic hours 1 Introduction to the course 4 2 Theoretical aspects of civil defence. The state system of a civil protection and the legislation of LR in the field of a civil protection. The rights and duties of citizens in the field of a civil protection. Scheduling of actions in the field of a civil protection. 4 3 Types of accidents. Possible accidents in Latvia. Actions of the population in case of accident. 4 4 System of alarm and notification. Evacuation of the population. The organization of evacuation actions in case of accident. 4 5 First aid 4 6 Fire safety 4 7 Global environmental problems: pollution, global warming, ozone depletion, climate change, acid rain, depletion of natural resources, waste disposal, deforestation and loss of biodiversity. 4 8 Environment protection in Latvia. Pollution of the environment as a result of economic activity. Legislation in the field of environment protection. 4 Total: 32 ac.h Description of students’ self-studies organization and assignments Self-study work Description Planned Learning Outcomes (PLO) % of final evaluation Students are required to study the indicated compulsory reading, sources, and methodological materials, as they are essential for understanding the fundamental concepts, completing assignments, and successfully mastering the course content. Detailed descriptions of each independent task and the assessment system are provided in the e-learning environment. 1. Individual PowerPoint Presentation on Disaster Management Students individually create and present a PowerPoint presentation covering disaster management, response strategies, evacuation plans, and case study analysis from real-life scenarios. Public speaking skills, presentation skills, analysis and synthesis of information, use of professional terminology, and ability to act correctly in different accidents and emergency situations (PLO 3, 4). 20% 2. Group work - PowerPoint presentation on Environment Protection Students work in groups to research and present environmental protection laws and policies in a country of their choice, comparing it with Latvian policies. Team-work, public speaking skills, presentation skills, analysis and synthesis of information, use of professional terminology, ability to ensure compliance with environmental protection legislation, and ability to apply normative legal acts regulating ecological safety issues (PLO 1, 2). 20% 3. Final test Comprehensive examination covering civil, environmental, and labor protection systems, first aid procedures, and emergency situation protocols. Comprehensive knowledge, skills and competences in civil protection, environmental safety, labor protection, fire safety, first aid, and ability to apply regulatory requirements in professional context (PLO 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). 60% Evaluation of mastering the study course Level Requirements Very high (10 –with distinction 9 – excellent) 10 (with distinction) - Knowledge, skills and competences exceed the requirements of the study course and demonstrate the ability to perform independent research as well as the deep understanding of problems. 9 (excellent) - Knowledge, skills and competences fully meet the requirements of the study course, student is able to apply the acquired knowledge independently. High (8 –very good 7 - good) 8 (very good) – The requirements of the study course are fully met, however, there is insufficient understanding of individual issues to use the knowledge independently for the solution of more complex problems. 7 (good) – The requirements of the study course are met in general, however, sometimes the inability to use the acquired knowledge independently is detected. Average (6 – almost good 5 – satisfactory 4 –almost satisfactory) 6 (almost good) – The requirements of the study course are met in general, however insufficient understanding of some problems and inability to apply the acquired knowledge is detected. 5 (satisfactory) – The requirements of the study course are met for the most part, however insufficient understanding of many problems and inability to apply the acquired knowledge is detected. 4 (almost satisfactory) – The requirements of the study course are met, for the most part, however insufficient understanding of some main concepts is detected as well as considerable difficulties in the practical application of the acquired knowledge are stated. Low (3 – 1 – negative evaluation) 3 (bad) – Knowledge is superficial and incomplete; the student is unable to use it in specific situations, 2 (very bad) – Superficial and incomplete knowledge of only some problems, the most part of the study course is not mastered. 1 (very very bad) – An absence of understanding of the main problems of the subject matter, almost no knowledge of the content of the study course.
